summary: Iteration 2 backend testing of NexoraOS: admin panel, Google auth endpoint, public QR ordering, and split payments. 23/23 pytest cases pass against the public preview URL. Focused only on the new features per E1's instruction; iteration-1 endpoints not re-tested.

minor.issue: When cafe_id is invalid the endpoint returns 404 (correct). But no validation that the table_id actually belongs to the same cafe until table lookup — currently query already scopes by cafe_id so this is fine. Note: order.notes concatenates raw customer_name/phone/notes without sanitisation — low-risk XSS if surfaced in UI without escaping.
public_create_order does NOT check subscription status of the target café — a café with an expired subscription can still receive public QR orders. Confirm if this is by design.

public_create_order does not deduct inventory or update customer stats; also does not require any rate-limit / CAPTCHA — a malicious client can spam orders anonymously. Consider basic per-IP rate limit.
total_revenue is summed in Python by loading up to 10,000 invoices with .to_list(10000); use a Mongo $group aggregation for scale.

N+1 pattern: for each café performs 4 additional queries (owner, subscription, staff_count, order_count). Fine for MVP; will not scale beyond a few hundred cafés — use aggregation with $lookup / $facet.
First-time Google signup auto-creates a café even when cafe_name is omitted (uses '{name}\'s Café'). No trial/plan validation, and no rate-limit on token attempts. Acceptable for MVP but flagging.

payment_splits amounts are not validated to sum to order.total. A cashier could enter splits that add up to more/less than the total and the order would still be marked 'paid'. Recommend server-side check: abs(sum(splits) - total) < 0.01 when payment_method='split'.

action_items: (Optional) Validate payment_splits sum == order.total server-side when payment_method='split'.
(Optional) Block public QR ordering when the café's subscription is expired.
(Optional) Add rate-limit or basic abuse protection on /api/public/orders.
(Optional) Replace N+1 loops in /api/admin/cafes and revenue sum in /api/admin/stats with Mongo aggregations.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 946 lines — split into routers/modules (auth, orders, menu, staff, subscription, admin, public).

OrderBody.create_order still trusts client-supplied item.price for authenticated orders (only public endpoint resolves price from DB). A rogue cashier token could underprice items. Consider resolving price server-side for authenticated /api/orders too.
public_create_order calls clean(doc) but ignores the return value (line 871); the returned dict is intentionally minimal so this is a dead call — remove it.
CORS middleware still uses allow_origins='*' with allow_credentials=True — invalid browser combo; must be tightened when frontend cookies are used.

Admin seed only updates password_hash+role when password mismatches; if admin email is manually flipped to a non-admin role in Mongo, seed will not restore admin role unless the password also changed. Consider always re-asserting role='admin' on startup.
google_login verify uses google.oauth2.id_token.verify_oauth2_token without clock_skew tolerance; may reject slightly-clock-skewed tokens.
payment_splits schema stores List[{method, amount}] but the server never validates 'method' enum (cash/upi/card). A client could send method='crypto' and it would persist.
